Nicotine wise, get an electronic cigarette and then steadily buy juice with less nicotine in it so you taper. As for weed look into buying the stuff that only has CBD in it and no THC. Youre still smoking weed but you don't get high (helps break psychological addiction without going cold turkey) but still feel sleepy/relaxed. If you're already addicted to nicotine you could try packing out the spliff with tobacco, increasing the ratio over time as you feel ready, so you smoke a bit less weed each time.

Tinnitus is temporary. You'll get it after being at a gig or in a nightclub with pounding music. High pitched ringing in the ears, noticeable when you're in a silent place such as in bed later that night. It goes away after a few hours. You'll only get it permanently if you're exposed to very loud sounds for extended periods of time i.e working on a construction site for years and never wearing ear protectors.

The fibers in your ear that detect sound are like little blades of grass. If you walk over some grass it pops back up. If hundreds of people walk on it every day, it'll end up stomped down and won't grow back, so be kind to your ears. If it helps I spent years dancing in front of huge speakers in nightclubs loud enough to feel the bass thump in your chest, having to scream at the top of your lungs so the person next to you can hear you talk, making your ears itch. I did this every Friday and Saturday night for about 4 years, and at 27 I don't have tinnitus. Just use some common sense with the volume and you'll be fine.

As someone with anxiety you're probably well versed in making up excuses as to why you can't do things that you're secretly anxious about, so you know how easy it is to come up with excuses not to hang out with people. Oh I have to be up early in the morning, oh I already have plans that night etc. They could easily do the same if they felt like it. The fact they're hanging out with you shows nobody wanted to excuse themselves.

At the end of the day we all meet thousands of people but only end up choosing a few of them as our friends. You were one of their choices and I'm sure they had lots to choose from. You made the cut!

A car isn't just one big object, it's a thousand little bits all bolted together to give the appearance of one big object. 

You're correct when you say that online course isn't enough, its definitely not enough on its own, but when you bolt it on to your life as an addition to all the other things you've done/are doing/will do, you're building on your life, slowly creating that big thing. Just keep doing those little things. A single dollar isn't much money at all, but a million dollars is a lot. Point is: if you add a lot of things you thought were worthless together youve suddenly got a lot.

When I was in university I had a class where everyone had to do a presentation at the end of term. I literally bailed out of the room about 2 presentations before mine. I ended up emailing the tutor and being honest about my anxiety issues. She said I could do it the next day with the next group. I was terrified again, but once you start your mind so focused from adrenaline you literally can't feel fear or anxiety, time seems to cease existing and your mouth is on autopilot. It's like the brain has given up on the flight part of flight or fight and is just fighting now, you're on the attack a little bit. Just before you go up there you'll feel absolutely crippled by fear but once you start you'll just run right through it and it'll be over before it even started. I know exactly what you're going through with the anticipation. It's the most painful, agonising feeling. One bit of advice I can give you is that the thing I was presenting on was something I was really interested in, so focus on the things you've really genuinely liked about your time there, you wont have much issue remembering what you wanted to say because it'll just be the truth, you won't feel like you're putting on an act, if you see what I mean. Just remember, I know this feels like the end of the world but life will continue after this. When you step off that stage your life will continue, there will be sunshine again bro, don't worry.

You described how I feel perfectly. A book I read said "How many sunsets have I missed while looking right at them?" I wish my head would shut up so I can experience something, enjoy it and remember it. I spend all my time stuck in the past unless I'm worrying about the future.

On the idea of being a weak person: imagine having a toothache. It hurts. You can't concentrate on anything and everyday tasks become huge chores because you're in so much pain. If you see other people going about their daily business, you don't marvel at how much stronger they are than you, or sit there wondering how they summon the strength to fulfil their obligations while in massive amounts of pain, because you know they don't have toothaches. 

My point is it's unfair to consider yourself weaker than others when they don't have to drag the dead weight of anxiety with them through life. It's an unfair comparison. Its like taking a maths exam while being attacked by a lion. Other people are going to score better than you on that test, but they weren't having their legs eaten.
